goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: The focused 38-test suite passes, encryption and acknowledgement degradation are sound, and offload never suppresses output. The milestone is nevertheless unsafe for graph work. Working state, pins, and tombstones are stored in one rewritable `state.json.aead`, contrary to the blueprint’s independent framed journals. Rebuild starts from capture events alone, resets pins/tombstones, and rewrites canonical episodes active, so projection corruption can resurrect deleted evidence. Read/mutation APIs bind only workspace plus opaque IDs, not the expected project/session, and rebuild trusts caller scope instead of validating every source record. Selection also preserves stale eviction status, producing a different result from rebuild. These are authority, isolation, and deletion-safety failures.

worker_package.objective: Repair the T004 Working Memory/Evidence Ledger milestone before any graph work. Replace the monolithic rewritable working state with the blueprint’s encrypted manifest plus independently framed, append-only evidence/checkpoint/tombstone mutation journals; each frame must carry sequence and previous-frame hash, use AEAD, fsync before acknowledgement, and support deterministic replay. Treat capture payloads and canonical episode records as authority while keeping Working indexes rebuildable; store only episode references in projections. Persist pin/unpin and tombstone mutations independently so corruption or deletion of derived state cannot lose them. Tombstones must be authoritative before episode/index projection changes, survive injected crashes, deny reopening immediately, and remain applied during every rebuild. Recompute selection from all eligible non-tombstoned records so incremental state and rebuild are identical, while preserving pins and explicit over-capacity state. Require and validate workspace, project, session, working-set, and evidence bindings on reads and mutations; validate every capture record during rebuild and reject cross-project/session records indistinguishably from unknown IDs. Validate fork parents in the same scope, make sibling forks distinct, and implement persisted opaque prefixed UUIDv7 working/evidence/episode identities while retaining stable resume and event idempotence. Preserve truthful capture acknowledgements, encrypted spool fail-open behavior, disabled-by-default compatibility, canonical payload non-duplication, and permanent offload non-replacement. Add adversarial tests for cross-scope access, forged rebuild scope, pin/tombstone survival, fault boundaries, journal corruption/truncation, deterministic selection/rebuild, sibling forks, and safe migration or explicit rejection of the interim T004 state format. Do not begin graph, ontology, improve, Active Map, MCP recall, lifecycle UI, installer, deployment, or production rollout.

stop_if: Any required implementation would overwrite, discard, or silently replace existing dirty user work instead of merging around it.
Pins or tombstones cannot survive loss or corruption of every derived manifest/index snapshot without treating an independently durable mutation journal as authority.
A tombstone can be acknowledged before its authoritative frame is fsynced, or a crash can leave any normal read path able to reopen the evidence.
Any read, mutation, fork, or rebuild can proceed without exact workspace, project, session, working-set, and evidence bindings or can reveal whether a foreign identifier exists.
Rebuild would trust caller-supplied project/session fields over canonical source envelopes, resurrect tombstoned episodes, lose pins, or produce different selection from incremental replay.
Supporting opaque UUIDv7 identities and stable resume would require rewriting canonical capture payloads or weakening event idempotence.
A durable or reopen-verified response could be emitted before capture, working evidence, canonical episode, and authoritative mutation state are fsynced and reopened with matching hashes and scope.
A partial, spooled, corrupt, expired, purged, tombstoned, or unverified capture could become offload-eligible or suppress original output.
Flags-off behavior changes, plaintext payloads are duplicated, physical paths leak, AEAD/frame chaining is weakened, or a projection becomes canonical.
A required change falls outside allowed_files or enters graph, ontology, improve, Active Map, MCP recall, lifecycle UI, installer, deploy, or production rollout.
Any deterministic test requires Ollama, Hindsight, Graphiti, Neo4j, credentials, a real user vault, or network writes.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.

evidence.findings: Working artifacts and canonical episodes are AEAD-encrypted, use private directories/files, and contain metadata/payload references rather than duplicated plaintext. Quota selection preserves pins, reports over-capacity, and leaves capture payloads intact. High-watermarks use max sequence and duplicate event admission reuses evidence.

`codex-working-set-store.mjs:127-221` persists manifest, entries, episodes, pins, and tombstones together in `state.json.aead`. Blueprint §10 requires separate manifest plus independently framed encrypted entries/checkpoints/tombstones journals with sequence and previous-frame hash. The implementation rewrites the entire blob on every mutation.

`tombstone` records deletion only inside the rewritable state and updates canonical episodes after the state commit. `rebuild` starts with empty state, reads capture events only, recreates every eligible entry and episode as active, resets pins, and overwrites episode files. Therefore corrupted derived state can resurrect tombstoned evidence and discard pin history.

`readState`, `openEvidence`, `readEpisode`, and mutation helpers require workspace plus opaque IDs but no expected project/session binding. `rebuild` filters capture records by workspace/session, never verifies each envelope’s project against the requested project, and writes caller-supplied scope into rebuilt entries and episodes.

`selectWorkingEvidence` seeds selection only from entries not already marked evicted. After capacity becomes available, previously evicted evidence remains evicted; a fresh rebuild starts every record selected and can choose differently. A direct check returned zero selected tokens despite 60 tokens of available capacity.

Capture commits the encrypted payload and journal before projecting Working Memory. Successful Working acknowledgements reopen payload and episode and compare hashes; injected post-state-commit failure returns `working.durable=false`, `reopen_verified=false`, and degraded state while retaining canonical capture. Daemon client falls back to the encrypted spool.

`evaluateWorkingOffload` rejects disabled, non-durable, incomplete, unverified, partial, spooled, corrupt, tombstoned, expired, purged, unselected, undersized, and non-allowlisted cases. Every receipt hard-codes `replacement_enabled:false` and `suppress_original:false`; adapters do not wire output replacement.

Fresh focused verification passes 38/38 tests, but the rebuild test corrupts a state containing neither pins nor tombstones, and scope tests do not attempt same-workspace cross-project/session access or forged rebuild scope. Existing green gates therefore do not exercise the unsafe paths.

PM supplied a fresh full `SuperMemory` index with 8,064 nodes, 12,972 edges, skipped_count=0, persistence=false. Exact findings were verified in source; broad search output was truncated and no exhaustive absence claim is made. Deploy remains excluded.

T004 reported changes within its approved allowed_files and no deviations. The repository remains dirty with substantial user-owned untracked work; this Judge made no source, state, index, staging, installation, or configuration changes.

parallel_safety.reason: Journal format, canonical episode authority, scope validation, selection replay, capture acknowledgements, and fault tests form one coupled durability contract across dirty files. Splitting writers risks incompatible migrations and deletion semantics.
